1. (Currently amended) A control system comprising:
a controller including a processor and memory, the controller being communicatively coupled to automation components in the control system and configured to facilitate performance of a process through interoperation with the automation components by generating holistic state data, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by:
determining a model configured to describe the process used by the controller;
determining input and output variables of the process;
determining constraints on the input and output variables;
determining an objective function associated with the process used by the controller; and
storing the model, the input and output variables, the constraints, and the objective function in one of a plurality of fields in the holistic state data to enable the automation components to detect and operate with the controller upon receiving the holistic state data, wherein the holistic state data is transmitted to the automation components to control physical operations of the process.

2. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a communication network and to communicate the holistic state data to each of the automation components upon connecting to the communication network, wherein the communication network transmits the holistic state data to control physical operations of the automation components.

3. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a backplane and to communicate the holistic state data to the automation components upon connecting to the backplane, wherein the backplane transmits the holistic state data to control physical operations of the automation components.

4. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the holistic state data is a standardized format understood by each of the automation components, and wherein the standardized format enables the automation components to interpret and execute control actions based on the holistic state data.

5. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by:
determining an intermediate search result of an optimization search;
determining a state of the optimization search when the intermediate search result is determined; and
storing the intermediate search result and the state in an optimization state field of the holistic state data, wherein the optimization search is performed to determine control actions that optimize the process.

6. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data to facilitate performing an optimization search in conjunction with one or more of the automation components in the control system, wherein the optimization search determines control actions to optimize performance of the process.

7. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data by:
determining computational capabilities of the controller;
determining interconnections with the automation components in the control system; and
storing the computational capabilities and the interconnections in a controller settings field of the holistic state data, wherein the computational capabilities and interconnections are used to determine how to distribute control operations among the automation components.

8. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to communicate the holistic state data to a server in the control system to facilitate determining an optimization problem, wherein the server uses the holistic state data to determine control actions that optimize the process.

9. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller comprises a processor, memory, and an in-memory database configured to store the holistic state data, wherein the in-memory database enables rapid access to the holistic state data for controlling the automation components.

10. (Currently amended) A tangible, non-transitory computer-readable medium configured to store instructions executable by a processor of a controller, wherein the instructions comprise instructions to:
receive, using the processor, control system configuration data;
determine, using the processor, automation components communicatively coupled to the controller and characteristics of the automation components based at least in part on the control system configuration data;
determine, using the processor, an optimization problem based at least in part on the automation components and the characteristics of each of the automation components;
instruct, using the processor, one or more of the automation components to perform a control action in a process, wherein the control action is determined based at least in part on the optimization problem and is transmitted to the automation components to control physical operations of the process.

11. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a model used by the automation component to control the process, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on the model used by each of the automation components.

12. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a computing capability of the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on computing capabilities of each of the automation components to distribute control operations.

13. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the control system configuration data comprises a plurality of holistic state data, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data corresponds with one of the automation components and describes the automation component's role in controlling the process.

14. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein the instructions to determine the automation components and characteristics of the automation components comprise instructions to parse each of the plurality of holistic state data to extract control-relevant information.

15. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data comprises a standardized format with same fields, wherein the standardized format enables the controller to interpret and use the holistic state data to control the automation components.

16. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the instructions to receive the configuration data comprise instructions to receive the configuration data from a cloud computing system, wherein the cloud computing system provides the configuration data to enable the controller to determine control actions for the automation components.

17. (Currently amended) A method for performing diagnostics on a control system comprising:
determining, using a processor, holistic state data captured by a controller in the control system, wherein the holistic state data describes a state of the control system;
simulating, using the processor, operation of the controller based at least in part on the holistic state data while the controller performs other operations, wherein the simulation predicts how the controller would respond to various conditions;
analyzing, using the processor, the simulation of the controller to perform diagnostics on the controller, wherein the analysis identifies potential issues with the controller's operation;
adjusting, using the processor, operation of the control system based at least in part on the diagnostics, wherein the adjustment modifies how the controller controls the automation components.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein:
simulating operation comprises simulating performance of various control actions by the controller on the automation components;
and analyzing the simulation comprises analyzing results of the various control actions to determine which control actions would optimize the process.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein analyzing the simulation comprises:
determining a predicted response to a control action determined by the controller using a model of the process;
and comparing the predicted result with an actual response to the control action to determine accuracy of the model, wherein the accuracy determines whether the model should be adjusted.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, comprising adjusting the model when the predicted response and the actual response vary by more than a threshold amount, wherein the adjusted model is used to determine future control actions.
